step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified core system entry points and actors: Customer (UserConsumerMobile) calling into Amazon Connect, and Agent (UserCompanyAgent) accessing the Amazon Connect console.
2. Identified media processing pipeline: Connect streams audio to Kinesis Video Streams, which feeds into Amazon Transcribe, persisting transcripts into DynamoDB.
3. Identified AI processing pipeline: DynamoDB transcript data feeds into Amazon Translate for real-time speech translation back to the Agent, and Amazon Comprehend for sentiment analysis/keyword extraction.
4. Identified persistent storage layer: Completed transcripts and analytics results are stored in Amazon S3.
5. Identified serverless compute node: Lambda is present on the whiteboard as part of the architecture logic.
6. Formatted all nodes using exact service vocabulary strings and sequential integer IDs, then structured directed flow edges.

edges.notes: Customer calls into Amazon Connect contact center.
Connect feeds live audio stream to Kinesis Video Streams.
Kinesis Video Streams feeds audio into Amazon Transcribe.
Transcribe writes generated text into DynamoDB.
DynamoDB feeds transcript text to Amazon Translate.
Translated text is delivered to agent console in real time.
DynamoDB feeds transcript text to Amazon Comprehend.
Sentiment and context insights are delivered to agent console.
Transcripts and AI insights are archived into S3 upon call completion.
